title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: Stripe
providers.scope_notes: Separate Dashboard SSO/session controls from key access policies. OAuth Connect and Apps are different authorization surfaces.

controls.name: Organization API key permissions
controls.what: Org keys can be restricted to read or write specific resources.
controls.quote: Restrict organization API keys to grant read or write permission to only specific resources.

controls_unknown: No account setting found to forbid creating unrestricted secret keys or to require key expiry.
Whether access policies and approval rules can be attached to organization API keys.
Whether uninstalling a Stripe App immediately revokes its OAuth refresh tokens is not stated.
Which organization roles can create org API keys or service principals, and how to disable a service principal.
Approval rules' actor condition for service principals is mentioned on the service principals page but not described on the approvals page.

authentication.summary: A secret key (prefix sk_org) created at the Stripe organization level and sent as a bearer token. Requests must include Stripe-Version, and Stripe-Context to name the target account; one key can reach any account in the organization.

federation.details: Static secret key; no external identity exchange is involved.

ip_restriction.boundary: Access policies (IPv4/CIDR, ASN, country, proxy/Tor blocking) are documented for account-level standard and restricted keys. The docs reviewed do not say whether they can be attached to organization keys.

lifetime.summary: No default expiration (stated for Stripe API keys generally)

renewal.summary: The same static key is reused on every request until it is expired or replaced; rotation and expiry steps are documented only for account-level keys.

administration.summary: Created and managed on the organization Dashboard's API keys tab; permissions can be restricted to read or write on specific resources. Organization-level roles apply to every account in the organization. Security history includes an API action category.
administration.conditions: Requires a Stripe organization with multiple accounts. Stripe advises using an organization key only for cross-account or organization operations. Which organization roles can create keys was not found.

offboard.details: Organization keys work at the organization level and are not tied to a user.

inventory.details: API keys tab of the organization Dashboard.

reads.ui: Workbench > Logs (organization); filter API endpoint /v1/balance, Method GET, Account

token_format.notes: All org keys use sk_org regardless of permissions (no rk_org). Body format not documented; regex is loose. No GitHub secret scanning pattern listed for sk_org.

log_sources.name: Workbench request logs (organization view)
log_sources.notes: Org-level logs identify which account in the organization each request/error applies to; filter by account, IP, endpoint, source.

log_sources.name: Activity Logs API
log_sources.notes: API key actions are per account (context); whether org-key lifecycle appears is not documented.

log_sources.name: Events (/v1/events)
log_sources.notes: Object changes in the targeted account; context field carries authentication context.

credential_id_fields.notes: If org keys are logged (not confirmed)

anomaly_cues: One sk_org key touching many accounts (Stripe-Context values) it normally never reaches
Stripe-Context using platform/connected path format (acct_x/acct_y) not seen before
Org key requests from IPs outside known servers
Org key used where only one account is needed (violates documented guidance) - review scope
Write calls (refunds, payouts) from an org key normally used for reporting

containment.steps: Organization Dashboard > API keys tab (org/api-keys/secret): rotate or expire the sk_org key; then review org-level Workbench logs per account.
containment.notes: Org-key rotate/expire semantics are not separately documented; assume same as account keys (7-day grace unless expired now).

sample_query.language: Stripe Events API (HTTP GET, org key)
sample_query.purpose: Per-account sweep of recent refunds to check for org-key misuse; repeat per Stripe-Context.

unknown: Org-key lifecycle events (Activity Logs coverage for sk_org)
Whether access policies apply to org keys
Request log field naming the org key used
Secret scanning partner coverage for sk_org

calls.reveals: Balance of any account in the organization
calls.log_notes: Workbench request log (Dashboard > Workbench > Logs), not Security history; retention not stated. Organization view identifies the target account.
